fixed_question: In the Probabilistic Allen Algebra (PAA) paper, how does the distribution-induced view differ from treating relation prediction as a flat classification problem over the thirteen Allen labels?
fixed_ground_truth: The distribution-induced view derives each relation's probability from how much of the distribution over the uncertain temporal quantities (point location, or interval midpoint and duration) falls in the region where that relation holds, so probabilities vary smoothly and distinguish configurations that one crisp label conflates. Prior work either assigns probabilities to relations directly or treats relation prediction as flat classification over the thirteen Allen labels, where crisp relations are brittle (a sub-threshold boundary shift flips the label) and inadequate (one label can cover markedly different configurations).
